examples.sr: Хвала, [на̀јео сам се], не могу више.
examples.en: Thanks, I'm full, I can't eat any more.

note: A woman says «најела сам се». Stronger than «сит сам».

examples.sr: Хвала, [до̏ста ми је], већ сам појео два парчета.
examples.en: Thanks, that's enough for me, I've already had two pieces.

note: Polite when about food; without context it means «I'm fed up»: «доста ми је свега».

examples.sr: Јави кад стижеш, да [ста̏вим ка̀фу].
examples.en: Let me know when you're coming, so I can put the coffee on.

note: An invitation for coffee. A question to a guest: «Какву пијеш?»

examples.sr: Хоћу да ти кажем нешто [у ве́зи са ти̏м].
examples.en: I want to tell you something about that.

note: The correct form is «у вези са тим»; «у вези тога» is a common mistake, even among native speakers.

examples.sr: Здраво! [Шта̏ и̏ма но̀во] код тебе?
examples.en: Hi! What's new with you?

note: Replies: «Ништа посебно», «Ево, радим». It's usual to ask back: «А код тебе?»

meanings: could be better (reply to «how are you?»)

examples.sr: - Како си? - [Би́ће бо̏ље̄].
examples.en: - How are you? - Could be better.

note: An evasive answer when things are not going well. Roughly «so-so».

meanings: to fall in love at first sight

examples.sr: [Заљу̀био сам се на пр̏ви по̏гле̄д].
examples.en: I fell in love at first sight.

note: A woman says «заљубила сам се».

examples.sr: Хвала ти, [ти ми улепша̀ваш да̑н].
examples.en: Thank you, you brighten my day.

note: A compliment, fine for friends too.

meanings: who's going to see you home?

examples.sr: Касно је, [ко̏ те пра̏ти ку̏ћи]?
examples.en: It's late, who's going to see you home?

note: A line from the cult film «Муње». In Serbia it is customary to walk a girl home after a date.

examples.sr: [Колѝко ће то̑ да ко̑шта] до аеродрома?
examples.en: How much will it cost to get to the airport?

note: Useful in a taxi: you can ask the price in advance.

meanings: can you turn on the air conditioning?

examples.sr: [Мо̏жете ли да укљу̀чите кли̑му], молим вас?
examples.en: Can you turn on the air conditioning, please?

note: Variant: «грејање» - heating.

key: phr:можете ли да ме одвезете до

examples.sr: [Мо̏жете ли да ме одвѐзете] до станице?
examples.en: Can you take me to the station?

note: A polite form; in a taxi, «возач» is the driver.

key: phr:тражи посао, а моли бога да га не нађе
meanings: he looks for a job but prays not to find one

examples.sr: Мој комшија [тра̏жи по̀сао, а мо̏ли Бо̀га да га не на̑ђе].
examples.en: My neighbor is looking for a job and praying he won't find one.

note: A joke about someone who is officially job hunting but doesn't want to find work.

meanings: I am writing to you regarding

examples.sr: [Пи̑ше̄м вам у ве́зи са] отварањем рачуна.
examples.en: I am writing to you regarding the opening of an account.

note: The start of a business letter; «са» takes the instrumental.

examples.sr: [У при̏логу вам ша̏ље̄м] тражена документа.
examples.en: I am attaching the requested documents.

note: In a letter, «Вам» is written with a capital letter.

examples.sr: Извините због кашњења, [хва́ла на разумѐвању].
examples.en: Sorry for the delay, thank you for your understanding.

note: A polite closing of a formal letter.

examples.sr: [Са пошто̀вањем], Марко Петровић
examples.en: Sincerely, Marko Petrović

note: The sign-off of a business letter; informally - «Све најбоље».

key: phr:боље врабац у руци него голуб на грани
meanings: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
forms: literally: better a sparrow in the hand than a pigeon on the branch

examples.sr: Узми што нуде, [бо̏ље̄ вра́бац у ру̀ци не̏го го̏лӯб на гра̑ни].
examples.en: Take what they're offering: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

key: phr:ко рано рани, две среће грабе
meanings: the early bird catches the worm
forms: literally: whoever rises early grabs two pieces of luck

examples.sr: Устајем у пет, јер [ко̏ ра̏но ра̑ни, две̑ сре̑ће гра̏бе].
examples.en: I get up at five because the early bird catches the worm.

forms: literally: without hardship there is no learning

examples.sr: Мораш да вежбаш, [без му̀ке нѐма нау̀ке].
examples.en: You have to practice: no pain, no gain.

key: phr:ко са ђаволом тикве сади, о главу му се разбијају
meanings: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas
forms: literally: whoever plants pumpkins with the devil, they get smashed on his head

examples.sr: Не дружи се с њима, [ко̏ са ђа̏волом ти̏кве са̏ди, о гла̑ву му се разбѝјају].
examples.en: Don't hang out with them: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas.

meanings: everything comes to those who wait

examples.sr: Не губи наду, [ко̏ чѐка, до̀чека].
examples.en: Don't lose hope: everything comes to those who wait.

key: phr:боље жива кукавица него мртав херој
meanings: better a live coward than a dead hero
forms: literally: better a living coward than a dead hero

examples.sr: Побегао је, јер [бо̏ље̄ жи̏ва ку̏кавица не̏го мр̀тав хѐро̄ј].
examples.en: He ran away, because it's better to be a live coward than a dead hero.

meanings: one swallow doesn't make a summer

examples.sr: Један добар резултат ништа не значи, [је̏дна ла́ста не чѝни про̀леће].
examples.en: One good result means nothing: one swallow doesn't make a summer.

key: phr:не можеш имати и овце и новце
meanings: you can't have your cake and eat it too
forms: literally: you can't have both the sheep and the money

examples.sr: Хоћеш и мир и победу? [Не мо̏жеш ѝмати и о̑вце и но̑вце].
examples.en: You want both peace and victory? You can't have your cake and eat it too.

note: It rhymes: овце - новце. Said when someone wants everything at once.

forms: literally: old love has no oblivion

examples.sr: Срео је прву љубав, [ста̑ра љу́бав забо̀рава нѐма].
examples.en: He met his first love: old love never dies.

key: phr:где има дима, има и ватре

examples.sr: Не верујем причама, али [где̏ и̏ма ди̏ма, и̏ма и ва̏тре].
examples.en: I don't believe the gossip, but where there's smoke, there's fire.

key: phr:не продаје се кожа док је медвед још у шуми
meanings: don't count your chickens before they hatch

examples.sr: Не троши новац унапред, [не про̀даје се ко̑жа до̏к је мѐдвед јо̏ш у шу̏ми].
examples.en: Don't spend the money in advance: don't count your chickens before they hatch.

examples.sr: [Хва́ла што̏ сте до̀шли] на састанак.
examples.en: Thank you for coming to the meeting.

note: The opening of a meeting or presentation.

meanings: I'd like to introduce to you

examples.sr: [Же̏лим да вам предста̀вим] нашег новог колегу.
examples.en: I'd like to introduce our new colleague.

key: phr:можемо ли да почнемо са састанком

examples.sr: [Мо̏жемо ли да по̀чнемо са саста̀нком]?
examples.en: Can we start the meeting?

key: phr:који је рок за овај пројекат
meanings: what's the deadline for this project?

examples.sr: [Ко̀јӣ је ро̏к за о̀ва̄ј про̀јекат]?
examples.en: What's the deadline for this project?

examples.sr: Колега је јуче [да̑о о̏тка̄з].
examples.en: My colleague quit yesterday.

note: Used both for an employee quitting and for an employer firing someone.

examples.sr: Морао сам да [у̏зме̄м боло̀вање] због грипа.
examples.en: I had to take sick leave because of the flu.

examples.sr: Често [ра̏дим прековрѐмено] крајем месеца.
examples.en: I often work overtime at the end of the month.

examples.sr: Фирма нуди [ра̑д од ку̏ће] два дана недељно.
examples.en: The company offers working from home two days a week.

note: Variant: «радити од куће».

examples.sr: Фирма је објавила ново [ра̑дно ме̏сто].
examples.en: The company has announced a new job opening.

examples.sr: Добио сам посао [на нео̀дре̄ђено вре́ме].
examples.en: I got a permanent job.

examples.sr: Уговор је [на о̀дре̄ђено вре́ме], годину дана.
examples.en: The contract is fixed-term, for one year.

examples.sr: Имамо [про̏бни ра̑д] од месец дана.
examples.en: We have a one-month probation period.

examples.sr: Добар дан, [занѝма ме о̀во̄ ра̑дно ме̏сто].
examples.en: Hello, I'm interested in this position.

meanings: do you have an appointment available?

examples.sr: Добар дан, [и̏мате ли сло̀бодан тѐрмӣн] сутра?
examples.en: Hello, do you have an appointment available tomorrow?

key: phr:желим да отворим рачун у банци
meanings: I want to open a bank account

examples.sr: [Же̏лим да отво̀рим ра̀чӯн у ба̏нци].
examples.en: I want to open a bank account.

examples.sr: Отворио сам [тѐкӯћӣ ра̀чӯн] у банци.
examples.en: I opened a checking account at the bank.

note: A savings account is «штедни рачун».

examples.sr: Желим да отворим [ште̏дни ра̀чӯн].
examples.en: I want to open a savings account.

meanings: are you paying cash or by card?

examples.sr: [Пла̀ћате ли ке̑шом и̏ли ка̏ртицом]?
examples.en: Are you paying cash or by card?

examples.sr: [Колѝко сам ду́жан]? - Хиљаду динара.
examples.en: How much do I owe? - A thousand dinars.

note: A woman says «Колико сам дужна?»

meanings: money is no problem, there just isn't any

examples.sr: Често кажу: [па̑ре ни́су про̀бле̄м, па̑ра нѐма].
examples.en: People often say: money is no problem, there just isn't any.

note: A pun: «паре» is money, «пара» is its genitive plural, so «пара нема» means «no money». A favorite Serbian joke.

examples.sr: Ништа ми не помаже, све је [џа̏бе].
examples.en: Nothing helps me, it's all in vain.

note: Also «for free». A Turkish loanword. Graffiti: «џабе кречили» - painted in vain.

meanings: how soon will the taxi come?

examples.sr: [За колѝко ће до́ћи та̀кси]?
examples.en: How soon will the taxi get here?

note: «За колико» means «in how much time».

examples.sr: Треба ми [ка̑рта у јѐдно̄м сме̑ру] до Ниша.
examples.en: I need a one-way ticket to Niš.

key: phr:боље празна кеса него празна глава
meanings: better an empty purse than an empty head

examples.sr: Учи, јер [бо̏ље̄ пра̀зна кѐса не̏го пра̀зна гла̀ва].
examples.en: Study, because it's better to have an empty purse than an empty head.

key: phr:паметни људи уче на туђим грешкама
meanings: smart people learn from other people's mistakes

examples.sr: [Па̏метнӣ љу̑ди у̏че на ту̑ђим гре̏шкама], будале на властитим.
examples.en: Smart people learn from other people's mistakes, fools from their own.

examples.sr: [Кѐса не тре́ба], хвала.
examples.en: No bag needed, thanks.

note: At the checkout you hear «Треба кеса?»

examples.sr: [Пола́ко], имамо времена.
examples.en: Take it easy, we have time.

note: A favorite Serbian word: «slowly», «don't rush» and «calm down» all in one.

meanings: to take the dog for a walk

examples.sr: Ако је лепо време, [извѐдем пса̏ у шѐтњу].
examples.en: If the weather is nice, I take the dog for a walk.

examples.sr: [Мо̑ј специјалѝте̄т је] гулаш са кромпиром.
examples.en: My specialty is goulash with potatoes.

examples.sr: Волим да кувам, [ужѝвам у про̀цесу].
examples.en: I like to cook, I enjoy the process.

examples.sr: [У колѝко ћемо се на́ћи] сутра?
examples.en: What time shall we meet tomorrow?

note: «У колико» means «at what time»; «наћи се» means «to meet up».

examples.sr: Вратио сам се кући у [јѐдан са̑т у̏јутру].
examples.en: I got home at one in the morning.

note: After midnight Serbian says «ујутру» (in the morning), not «ноћу»: «у три ујутру».

key: phr:од девет ујутру до шест увече
meanings: from nine in the morning to six in the evening

examples.sr: Радим [од де̏вет у̏јутру до ше̑ст у̏вече̄].
examples.en: I work from nine in the morning to six in the evening.

note: Parts of the day: ујутру, поподне, увече; «ноћу» is the dead of night.

examples.sr: Моја сестра је прави [књѝшки мо́љац].
examples.en: My sister is a real bookworm.

examples.sr: Он је [књѝшки мо́љац], све слободно време чита.
examples.en: He's a bookworm, he reads all his free time.

note: Serbian has a «moth» in the books where English has a worm.

meanings: it's better to know how than to have
skills are worth more than possessions

examples.sr: Моја бака каже: [бо̏ље̄ је у̀мети не̏го ѝмати].
examples.en: My grandmother says: it's better to know how than to have.

examples.sr: Улажи у знање, [бо̏ље̄ је у̀мети не̏го ѝмати].
examples.en: Invest in knowledge: it's better to know how than to have.

note: A proverb about learning.

key: phr:старо куче се не учи да лаје
meanings: you don't teach an expert his own job
don't teach your grandmother to suck eggs
forms: literally: you don't teach an old dog to bark

examples.sr: Не објашњавај му посао, [ста̀ро ку̏че се не у̏чи да ла̏је̄].
examples.en: Don't explain his job to him: you don't teach an old dog to bark.

examples.sr: Он то ради тридесет година, [ста̀ро ку̏че се не у̏чи да ла̏је̄].
examples.en: He's been doing this for thirty years, you don't teach an old dog to bark.

examples.sr: Цена је био главни [ка̏ме̄н спотѝцања] у преговорима.
examples.en: Price was the main stumbling block in the negotiations.

examples.sr: Језик му је највећи [ка̏ме̄н спотѝцања].
examples.en: Language is his biggest stumbling block.

meanings: to have a heart of stone
forms: literally: to have a heart of stone

examples.sr: Он [и̏ма ср̏це од камѐна], не жали никога.
examples.en: He has a heart of stone, he pities no one.

examples.sr: Мораш да [и̏маш ср̏це од камѐна] да то урадиш.
examples.en: You'd have to have a heart of stone to do that.

key: phr:камен ми је пао са срца
forms: literally: a stone fell from my heart

examples.sr: Положио сам испит и [ка̏ме̄н ми је па̑о са ср̑ца].
examples.en: I passed the exam and it was a weight off my mind.

examples.sr: Кад је јавила да је стигла, [ка̏ме̄н ми је па̑о са ср̑ца].
examples.en: When she let me know she had arrived, it was such a relief.

note: The pronoun changes with the person: «камен му је пао са срца».

examples.sr: Поверење је [ка̏ме̄н теме́љац] сваке везе.
examples.en: Trust is the cornerstone of every relationship.

examples.sr: Образовање је [ка̏ме̄н теме́љац] друштва.
examples.en: Education is the cornerstone of society.

note: You can also say just «темељ».

meanings: once upon a time (opening of a fairy tale)

examples.sr: [Би̏ла јѐдно̄м је̏дна] принцеза у далеком краљевству.
examples.en: Once upon a time there was a princess in a faraway kingdom.

examples.sr: Бака је почела причу: [би̏ла јѐдно̄м је̏дна] мала девојчица.
examples.en: Grandma began the story: once upon a time there was a little girl.

note: For a masculine noun: «био једном један». Other openings: «некада давно», «живели су једном».

key: phr:и живели су дуго и срећно
meanings: and they lived happily ever after (end of a fairy tale)
forms: literally: and they lived long and happily

examples.sr: Венчали су се и [жи́вели су ду̏го и сре̑ћно].
examples.en: They got married and lived happily ever after.

examples.sr: Бајка се завршава речима: и [жи́вели су ду̏го и сре̑ћно].
examples.en: The fairy tale ends with the words: and they lived happily ever after.

note: Variant: «живели су срећно до краја живота».

forms: literally: to me the nose is stuffed

examples.sr: Имам кијавицу, [за̀чепљен ми је но̑с].
examples.en: I have a cold, my nose is blocked.

examples.sr: Ноћу не могу да спавам јер [за̀чепљен ми је но̑с].
examples.en: I can't sleep at night because my nose is blocked.

examples.sr: [Сабѐри се], имаш још један испит.
examples.en: Pull yourself together, you have one more exam.

examples.sr: Престани да кукаш и [сабѐри се].
examples.en: Stop whining and pull yourself together.

note: Colloquial; the polite or plural form is «саберите се».

examples.sr: Студенти често [ра̏де хонора̀рно].
examples.en: Students often work part-time.

examples.sr: Желим да [ра̏дим хонора̀рно] док учим.
examples.en: I want to work part-time while I study.

note: Similar: «радити са скраћеним радним временом» - on reduced hours.

examples.sr: Отворио је радњу и сада [ра̏ди за са̀мог се̏бе].
examples.en: He opened a shop and now works for himself.

examples.sr: Једног дана желим да [ра̏дим за са̀мог се̏бе].
examples.en: One day I want to work for myself.

note: A woman says «за саму себе».

examples.sr: О селидби [ѝма̄м помѐшана осѐћања].
examples.en: I have mixed feelings about the move.

examples.sr: После финала [и̏мала је помѐшана осѐћања].
examples.en: After the final she had mixed feelings.

examples.sr: - Како ти иде учење? - [Ѝде не̏ка̄ко].
examples.en: - How's school going? - So-so.

examples.sr: Посао [ѝде не̏ка̄ко], али није лако.
examples.en: Work is getting along somehow, but it isn't easy.

note: A casual reply without enthusiasm.

meanings: all that work was for nothing

examples.sr: Поново је пљуснула киша, [џа̏бе смо крѐчили].
examples.en: It poured again, we painted for nothing.

examples.sr: На тек окреченом зиду неко је написао: [џа̏бе сте крѐчили].
examples.en: Someone wrote on the freshly whitewashed wall: you whitewashed for nothing.

note: Such graffiti appear on whitewashed walls; «џабе» means «in vain».

meanings: we'll be in touch (after an interview)

examples.sr: Хвала на разговору, [јавѝћемо вам се] у најскорије време.
examples.en: Thank you for the conversation, we will be in touch very soon.

examples.sr: [Јавѝћемо вам се] до петка.
examples.en: We'll get back to you by Friday.

note: A polite formula used by employers.

key: phr:не могу да се одвојим од књиге
meanings: I can't put the book down
forms: literally: I can't tear myself away from the book

examples.sr: Била је тако занимљива да [ни́сам мо̏гла да се одво̀јим од књѝге].
examples.en: It was so interesting that I couldn't put the book down.

examples.sr: Цео викенд [ни́сам мо̏гао да се одво̀јим од књѝге].
examples.en: I couldn't put the book down all weekend.

forms: literally: come on, let's not lose time

examples.sr: [Ха̀јде да не гу̏бимо вре́ме], почнимо одмах.
examples.en: Let's not waste time, let's start right away.

examples.sr: Воз касни, [ха̀јде да не гу̏бимо вре́ме] и узмимо такси.
examples.en: The train is late, let's not waste time and take a taxi.

note: Variant: «немојмо да губимо време».

examples.sr: Ова прича се преноси [с ко̀лена на ко̀лено].
examples.en: This story is passed down from generation to generation.

examples.sr: Рецепт се чува [с ко̀лена на ко̀лено].
examples.en: The recipe has been handed down through the generations.

forms: literally: here I am for you

examples.sr: Не брини, [ту̑ сам] за тебе.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'm here for you.

note: The main phrase of support. Similar: «Уз тебе сам», «Можеш да рачунаш на мене».

forms: literally: you can count on me

examples.sr: Увек [мо̏жеш да рачу̀наш на ме̏не].
examples.en: You can always count on me.

note: The verb «рачунати» takes «на» + acc.: to count on someone.

forms: literally: everything will be in order

examples.sr: Смири се, [све̏ ће бѝти у ре̑ду].
examples.en: Calm down, everything will be fine.

note: «У реду» also means «OK, fine» as a reply.

forms: literally: it is heavy for me on the heart

examples.sr: После свађе ми је [те̑шко на ср̑цу].
examples.en: After the quarrel my heart is heavy.

note: Impersonal: the person is in the dative («ми»), «тешко» has no subject.

forms: literally: to throw out of the track

examples.sr: Та вест ме је [изба̀цила из колосѐка].
examples.en: That news threw me off track.

note: «Колосек» is a railway track; compare «to go off the rails».

examples.sr: Лепа је хаљина, али [нѝје мо̑ј сти̏л].
examples.en: It's a beautiful dress, but it's not my style.

note: A polite way to decline without criticizing the item.

forms: literally: it does not answer to me

examples.sr: Овај термин ми [не одго̀вара].
examples.en: That time slot doesn't work for me.

note: «Одговарати» takes the dative: to suit someone. Also: «Одговара ми поподне».

meanings: I'd like to book an appointment
forms: literally: I would like (f.) to schedule a slot

examples.sr: [Же̏лела бих да зака̀жем тѐрмӣн] за петак.
examples.en: I'd like to book an appointment for Friday.

note: A man says «желео бих». «Термин» here is an appointment, a time slot.

meanings: Easter greeting and its reply: Christ is risen! - Truly, He is risen!
forms: literally: Christ has risen! - Indeed He has risen!

examples.sr: [Хрѝстос ва̏скрсе!] - Ваистину васкрсе!
examples.en: Christ is risen! - Truly, He is risen!

note: Said at Easter instead of «hello» and before the festive table; «Happy Easter» is «Срећан Васкрс!».

forms: literally: I have a booked slot

examples.sr: Добар дан, [ѝма̄м зака̀зан тѐрмӣн] у десет.
examples.en: Hello, I have an appointment at ten.

note: Works for a doctor, hairdresser or vet: «термин» is the time you are booked for.

forms: literally: my pet is not well

examples.sr: Хитно је, [мо̑ј љуби́мац нѝје до̀бро].
examples.en: It's urgent, my pet is not well.

note: «Љубимац» is a pet. For people: «Није ми добро» - I don't feel well.

examples.sr: [Прѝмате ли ка̏ртице] или само готовину?
examples.en: Do you accept cards, or only cash?

note: A question in a shop or cafe; «готовина» is cash.

forms: literally: I need a bigger number

examples.sr: Ове ципеле су тесне, [тре́ба ми ве̏ћӣ бро̑ј].
examples.en: These shoes are tight, I need a bigger size.

note: A shoe or clothing size is «број» (or «величина»). «Мањи број» - a smaller size.

examples.sr: [Да ли је спра̑ва сло̀бодна?] Хоћу да вежбам леђа.
examples.en: Is this machine free? I want to work on my back.

note: «Справа» is a gym machine; it also means a device or piece of apparatus.

forms: literally: turn to the left / to the right

examples.sr: Када прођете семафор, [скрѐните де̏сно].
examples.en: After you pass the traffic light, turn right.

note: The start of directions: «Наставите право, док не видите...» - keep going straight until you see...

meanings: where do I need to change?
forms: literally: where do I need to change seats?

examples.sr: [Где̏ тре́ба да пресѐдам] за Суботицу?
examples.en: Where do I need to transfer for Subotica?

note: Other useful questions: «Која је следећа станица?», «Да ли овај аутобус стаје на тргу?».

forms: literally: how much do I owe (m. / f.)?

examples.sr: Извините, [колѝко сам ду́жан]?
examples.en: Excuse me, how much do I owe?

note: Said in a cafe or shop when paying. The ending shows the speaker's gender: дужан - man, дужна - woman.

examples.sr: [Извѝни, ка̏сним] десет минута.
examples.en: Sorry, I'm running ten minutes late.

note: «Каснити» means to be late, now or in the future: «Касним десет минута».

examples.sr: Вечерас [ѝдемо на бле̏ју] у парк.
examples.en: Tonight we're going to hang out in the park.

note: Slang. Also «возити бајс» - to ride a bike (from «bike»); standard: «возити бицикл».

examples.sr: [Потпѝшите о́вде] и овде, молим вас.
examples.en: Sign here and here, please.

note: A formula from the office and the bank. Related: «Фали вам фотокопија пасоша» - you are missing a copy of your passport.

forms: literally: you have a wonderful smile

examples.sr: [И̏маш пре̏дӣван о̏сме̄х], знаш ли то?
examples.en: You have a lovely smile, you know that?

note: A sincere compliment, fine among acquaintances and in a romantic setting.

forms: literally: to run from the lesson

examples.sr: Лука данас сигурно [бѐжи са фѝзике].
examples.en: Luka will surely skip physics today.

note: Colloquial. «Час» is a lesson; the subject goes «са физике, са математике» (са + gen.).

examples.sr: Извините, [ѝма̄м са̏мо кру̑пно], немам ситно.
examples.en: Sorry, I only have large bills, I have no small change.

note: A courier or seller says it when they have no change. Compare «немам ситно» - I have no small change.

meanings: what do you do for a living?
forms: literally: what are you by occupation?

examples.sr: [Шта̏ си ти по занѝмању?] - Ја сам новинар.
examples.en: What do you do for a living? - I'm a journalist.

note: The answer: «Ја сам ... по занимању». Feminine forms: докторица, учитељица, новинарка.

key: phr:причај српски да те цео свет разуме
forms: literally: speak Serbian so that the whole world understands you

examples.sr: Ако хоћеш да те разумеју, [при̑чај ср̏пскӣ да те це̏о све̑т ра̏зӯме].
examples.en: If you want people to understand you, speak Serbian and the whole world will understand you.

note: A joking saying, as if everybody could understand Serbian.

examples.sr: Тамо станове купују само [тру̏лӣ бога̀таши].
examples.en: Only filthy rich people buy apartments there.

note: A colloquial intensifier: «трули» + noun, admiring and ironic. «Богаташ» is a rich man.

forms: literally: ready like a cocked rifle

examples.sr: Ја сам [спре̏ман ка̏о за̀пета пу̏шка], можемо да кренемо.
examples.en: I'm completely ready, we can set off.

note: The image of a cocked gun, but here with no negative tone: the person is ready to act.

meanings: the spitting image of one's father

examples.sr: Ти си [пљу̏нути о̀тац], ни ти никог не слушаш.
examples.en: You're the spitting image of your father: you don't listen to anyone either.

note: Said of a likeness to one's father, in character or in looks.

examples.sr: [Ола̀ди бре̏], не могу сад да причам!
examples.en: Back off, I can't talk right now!

note: Slang, probably from «охладити» (to cool off). Said to acquaintances, sounds rude. «Бре» is an intensifier.

forms: literally: a meter and a Gillette

examples.sr: Он је [ме̏тар и жѝлет], али игра кошарку.
examples.en: He's a shorty, but he plays basketball.

note: «Жилет» (Gillette) is a razor blade: a meter plus a blade. Variant «метар и шумска јагода». Often mocking.

examples.sr: Нико не прича, а ти си опет [пу̏стио тѝхомира].
examples.en: Nobody is talking, and you've let one go again.

note: Тихомир is a name: the joke is that he sneaks up quietly. Similar: «пустити голуба».

meanings: cash cow (a person who gets milked for money)

examples.sr: Он ради у иностранству, права [кра̏ва му̀зара].
examples.en: He works abroad, a real cash cow.

note: Said of someone who earns and spends on others, often someone working abroad. Joking, sometimes envious.

examples.sr: [Сре̏ћан Ва̑скрс] свима!
examples.en: Happy Easter, everyone!

examples.sr: [Сре̑ћна] вам слава!
examples.en: Wishing you a happy slava!

note: A pattern for holiday greetings: срећан / срећна / срећно + the holiday. The adjective agrees with the holiday: срећан Божић, срећна Нова година, срећан рођендан, срећан Васкрс.

examples.sr: Мој брат ради [пре̏ко ба̑ре].
examples.en: My brother works across the pond.

examples.sr: Многи су отишли [пре̏ко ба̑ре] за послом.
examples.en: Many people went across the pond for work.

note: «Бара» is a pond; a joking name for the Atlantic. Slang, often about the USA.

meanings: extremely heavy, gloomy (of a day, a period)

examples.sr: Дан је био [те̏жак ка̏о цр̀на зѐмља].
examples.en: The day was as heavy as black earth.

examples.sr: Ова недеља је [те̏шка ка̏о цр̀на зѐмља].
examples.en: This week is as heavy as black earth.

note: A comparison with wet, heavy soil. The adjective agrees with the subject.

meanings: the world has never seen this
forms: literally: the world has not seen this

examples.sr: [О̀во̄ све̑т нѝје ви̑део], опет нема струје!
examples.en: Unbelievable, the power is out again!

note: A grumbling, joking reaction to a series of troubles.

forms: literally: I have nothing to put on

examples.sr: Идем на свадбу, а [не̑ма̄м шта̏ да обу̀чем]!
examples.en: I'm going to a wedding and I have nothing to wear!

note: The pattern «немам + question word + да + present» means «nothing / no one to...»: «немам шта да једем» (nothing to eat), «немам с ким да причам» (no one to talk to).

key: phr:да ми је неко причао, не бих веровао
meanings: I wouldn't have believed it if someone had told me
forms: literally: if someone had told me, I would not believe

examples.sr: [Да ми је нѐко при̑чао, не бих ве̏ровао]!
examples.en: If someone had told me, I wouldn't have believed it!

note: An unreal condition: «да» + past tense in the if-clause, the conditional («не бих веровао») in the result.

examples.sr: Нисмо се видели [ме̏тар да̑на].
examples.en: We haven't seen each other in ages.

examples.sr: Пре [ме̏тар да̑на] сам почео да учим српски.
examples.en: I started learning Serbian ages ago.

note: Belgrade slang, often said as a joke.

examples.sr: [У ве́зи са] вашим последњим писмом, јављамо вам се.
examples.en: Regarding your last letter, we are getting in touch with you.

note: A formal opening in letters. Followed by the instrumental: «у вези са уговором».

examples.sr: [У при̏логу] шаљемо потребна документа.
examples.en: Please find the necessary documents attached.

note: A polite business expression. «Прилог» is an attachment.

examples.sr: [Ср̏да̄чан по̏здра̄в], Марко Петровић.
examples.en: Kind regards, Marko Petrović.

note: A standard sign-off of a business letter. A letter opens with «Поштовани господине...».

examples.sr: [У̀напре̄д за́хва̄лан] на вашем одговору.
examples.en: Thank you in advance for your reply.

note: Feminine: «унапред захвална». Used in a business letter after a request.

examples.sr: Тренер [што̏па вре́ме] на стази.
examples.en: The coach is timing the runners on the track.

note: From «штоперица» - a stopwatch; a colloquial verb.

examples.sr: Донећу ти књигу сутра, [завршѐно ти је то̑].
examples.en: I'll bring you the book tomorrow, consider it done.

note: A Montenegrin phrase. It all depends on the tone: from a reliable person it means «I'll definitely do it», from a lazy one it's an excuse. «Завршено је» just means «it's finished».

examples.sr: Остала сам [без пребијѐне па̑ре] после викенда.
examples.en: I was left without a penny after the weekend.

note: «Пребијена пара» is a cracked, worthless coin. Said of having no money at all.

examples.sr: Месец је тек почео, а ја сам већ [на ну̀ли].
examples.en: The month has only just started and I'm already broke.

note: Colloquial; in slang also «без кинте», «декинтиран».

forms: literally: a cobweb in the wallet

examples.sr: Погледао сам у новчаник, а тамо је само [па̏учина].
examples.en: I looked in my wallet and there were only cobwebs.

note: A joking image: there has been no money in the wallet for so long that a cobweb has grown.

meanings: to crawl along at a snail's pace
forms: literally: to drag oneself like a cow

examples.sr: Хајде, [ву́че̄ш се ка̏о кра̏ва]!
examples.en: Come on, you're moving at a snail's pace!

note: A reproach to a slow person. Serbs often swear with animal names: магарац (donkey, stupidity), свиња (slob, miser), змија (sly), овца (mindless follower).

examples.sr: [Не бу̏ди о́вца], размишљај својом главом!
examples.en: Don't be a sheep, think for yourself!

note: «Овца» is someone who follows the majority.

examples.sr: - Долазиш ли? - [Са̏д ћу]!
examples.en: - Are you coming? - Be right there!

note: Written as two words, «сад ћу», not «сају» or «sacu» - those are text-message shortcuts and look sloppy.

examples.sr: Колико спаваш? - [Ка̀ко ка̏д].
examples.en: How much do you sleep? - It depends.

note: Word order matters: not «кад како». Likewise «мање-више», not «више-мање».

examples.sr: Није дошао, [са̀мим ти̏м] ништа не зна.
examples.en: He didn't come, so he doesn't know anything.

note: Fixed word order: «самим тим», never «тим самим».

examples.sr: После свађе [о̑стао је го́рак у̀кус].
examples.en: The argument left a bitter taste.

note: Other variants: «остала је горчина», «остао је непријатан/нелагодан осећај», «остао је лош утисак».

meanings: blind drunk (a slang scale: «као летва», «као земља», «као бетон»)

examples.sr: Вратио се кући [пѝјан ка̏о зѐмља].
examples.en: He came home blind drunk.

note: Slang: «летва» - drank a lot, «земља» - even more, «бетон» - can't stand at all. All three are well above average.

examples.sr: После ракије је био [пѝјан ка̏о бѐто̄н].
examples.en: After the rakija he was dead drunk.

note: The top of the three slang steps: «летва», «земља», «бетон».

key: phr:упала му је кашика у мед
forms: literally: the spoon fell into honey for him

examples.sr: Нашао је посао одмах, [у̏пала му је ка̀шика у ме̑д].
examples.en: He found a job right away, he got lucky.

note: Old-fashioned, sounds formal to young people. Neutral: «Посрећило му се». There are crude slang variants too.

forms: literally: mothers still give birth to Obilićs

examples.sr: Спасио је дете из ватре, [јо̏ш ра̑ђају ма̑јке О̀билиће]!
examples.en: He saved a child from a fire: heroes are not extinct!

note: Miloš Obilić is a hero of the Kosovo legend. The phrase praises a brave act.

forms: literally: come on, you figure it out

examples.sr: Где је отишао? [А̏ј га зна̑ј]!
examples.en: Where did he go? Who the hell knows!

note: Not vulgar. Instead of «га» you can hear «ти» or «му».

key: phr:а шта кажеш на то што
meanings: and what about the fact that...? (a reproach in youth slang)
forms: literally: and what do you say to the fact that

examples.sr: [А шта̏ ка̏жеш на то̑ што̏] те сви сматрају лудом?
examples.en: And what do you say to the fact that everybody thinks you're crazy?

examples.sr: Ти си Сергеј, [је л' да]?
examples.en: You're Sergey, right?

note: A tag question added at the end of a statement; short for «је ли да». Belgraders hear it as «елда».

meanings: a men's clipper cut with short sides

examples.sr: Фризер ми је направио [ке̑ц-тро̏јку].
examples.en: The barber gave me a number one-three clipper cut.

examples.sr: Сви у екипи носе [ке̑ц-тро̏јку].
examples.en: Everybody on the team has the same clipper cut.

note: Named after the clipper guard numbers: «кец» (one) and «тројка» (three). Popular since the 90s as a practical cut.

examples.sr: [Ша́ла на стра̑ну], шта ћемо сада?
examples.en: Joking aside, what do we do now?

examples.sr: [Ша́ла на стра̑ну], ово је озбиљно.
examples.en: Joking aside, this is serious.

note: Used to move from jokes to business.

key: phr:ко воли окрајак, добиће добру ташту
meanings: whoever likes the heel of the loaf will get a good mother-in-law

examples.sr: Увек једе окрајак: [ко̏ во̀ли о̏крајак, доби́ће до̀бру та̏шту].
examples.en: He always eats the heel of the loaf: whoever likes it will get a good mother-in-law.

note: A joking superstition about the end of a loaf. Regions have different words for «окрајак»: крајка, пупушка, попак.

examples.sr: На језеру смо видели плавог [ви̏линог ко̀њица].
examples.en: We saw a blue dragonfly at the lake.

examples.sr: Дете јури [ви̏линог ко̀њица] по ливади.
examples.en: The child is chasing a dragonfly across the meadow.

note: Literally «fairy's horse»: «вила» is a fairy from Slavic legends. It's the ordinary Serbian word for a dragonfly.

examples.sr: Узми [фра̀нцуски кљу̑ч], овај завртањ је велики.
examples.en: Take the adjustable wrench, this bolt is big.

note: Plain «кључ» is both a door key and a wrench; the adjustable one is called «француски кључ».

examples.sr: Замотај жицу [изо̀лир тра̏ком].
examples.en: Wrap the wire with electrical tape.

note: The everyday name, at home and in shops.

examples.sr: Волим [мо̑рске пло̀дове], нарочито лигње.
examples.en: I like seafood, especially squid.

note: Literally «sea fruits». Used on menus; fish is usually listed separately.

forms: literally: to speak into the wind

examples.sr: Колико год му објашњаваш, [го̀ворӣш у ве̏тар].
examples.en: No matter how much you explain to him, you're wasting your breath.

examples.sr: Нико не слуша, као да [го̀ворӣм у ве̏тар].
examples.en: Nobody is listening, it's as if I'm talking to the wind.

note: An idiom about useless words: nobody hears them.

forms: literally: to shoot into the wind

examples.sr: Његови планови су [пу̏ца̄ње у ве̏тар].
examples.en: His plans are pie in the sky.

examples.sr: Без новца само [пу̏цамо у ве̏тар].
examples.en: Without money we're just spinning our wheels.

note: Effort is spent, but there is no target.

forms: literally: to fly by like the wind

examples.sr: Лето је [пролѐтело ка̏о ве̏тар].
examples.en: The summer flew by.

examples.sr: Година је [пролѐтела ка̏о ве̏тар].
examples.en: The year flew by.

note: Said of time that went by too quickly.

meanings: to act against one's own interest
forms: literally: to pee against the wind

examples.sr: Свађати се са шефом је као [пѝшати уз ве̏тар].
examples.en: Arguing with your boss is like peeing into the wind.

note: A colloquial, rather crude idiom: the result will be the opposite and unpleasant. Not for formal speech.

forms: literally: I have no slight connection

examples.sr: [Не̑ма̄м бла̀ге ве̑зе] како то ради.
examples.en: I have no idea how it works.

examples.sr: О рачунарима [не̑ма̄м бла̀ге ве̑зе].
examples.en: I haven't got a clue about computers.

note: A colloquial, more emphatic variant of «немам појма». Here «благ» means «slightest».

meanings: agreement is what builds a home

examples.sr: [До̏гово̄р ку̏ћу гра̏ди], хајде да се договоримо.
examples.en: Agreement builds a home, so let's come to an agreement.

note: A proverb: a household stands on agreement. Related: «без збора нема договора».

meanings: without discussion there is no agreement
forms: literally: without an assembly there is no agreement

examples.sr: Сви ћемо седети и причати: [без збо̏ра нѐма до̀говора].
examples.en: We'll all sit down and talk: without discussion there is no agreement.

note: «Збор» is an assembly, the council of a village community; the proverb says an agreement comes from talking together.

key: phr:где је слога, ту је и божји благослов
meanings: where there is harmony, there is God's blessing

examples.sr: [Где̏ је сло̏га, ту̑ је и бо̏жјӣ бла̏госло̄в], зато се не свађајте.
examples.en: Where there is harmony, there is God's blessing, so don't quarrel.

note: A proverb about peace in a family and a community; in the ijekavian variant «ђе је слога». Given here in the ekavian form.

forms: literally: a dumpling in the throat

examples.sr: Кад је чуо вест, остала му је [кне́дла у гр̏лу].
examples.en: When he heard the news, he was left with a lump in his throat.

examples.sr: Стоји ми [кне́дла у гр̏лу].
examples.en: I have a lump in my throat.

note: From tears and emotion; it can also have a medical sense - difficulty swallowing. «Кнедла» is a ball of dough, a dumpling.

key: phr:трава је увек зеленија у туђем дворишту
meanings: the grass is always greener on the other side
forms: literally: the grass is always greener in someone else's yard

examples.sr: Увек ти је [тра́ва зелѐнија у ту̑ђем дво̀ришту].
examples.en: For you, the grass is always greener on the other side.

examples.sr: Кажу да је [тра́ва зелѐнија ко̑д ко̀мшије].
examples.en: They say the grass is greener at the neighbor's.

note: The place can vary: «у комшије», «у туђој башти», «са друге стране ограде».

examples.sr: Деда је и у осамдесетој [здра̏в ка̏о дре̏н].
examples.en: Grandpa is healthy as a horse even at eighty.

examples.sr: После одмора сам [здра̏в ка̏о дре̏н].
examples.en: After the vacation I'm fit as a fiddle.

note: «Дрен» is the cornelian cherry, a tree with very hard wood.

meanings: like a chicken with its head cut off
forms: literally: a fly without a head

examples.sr: Лута као [му̀ва без гла̀ве] по граду.
examples.en: He wanders around the city like a chicken with its head cut off.

examples.sr: Радим као [му̀ва без гла̀ве] и ништа не завршавам.
examples.en: I'm working like a headless chicken and finishing nothing.

note: Said of a person whose actions are chaotic and aimless; often about a beginner behind the wheel.

examples.sr: Не жури, [стр̏пљен - спа̏шен].
examples.en: Don't rush: patience pays off.

note: A proverb for situations where you can't get what you want right away. People joke that its meaning is clearest when the toilet is occupied.

meanings: from a needle to a locomotive
forms: literally: from a needle to a locomotive

examples.sr: У хипермаркету се може купити [од и̏гле до локомотѝве].
examples.en: In a hypermarket you can buy everything from a needle to a locomotive.

note: Said of a market or a store that has absolutely everything.

forms: literally: to put end to end

examples.sr: Једва [саста̀вљам кра̑ј са кра̏јем].
examples.en: I can barely make ends meet.

examples.sr: Како [саста̀вљате кра̑ј са кра̏јем] до плате?
examples.en: How do you make ends meet until payday?

note: An expression about running short of money before payday.

forms: literally: not hesitating for an hour

examples.sr: [Не ча̀сећи ни ча̏са], лисица је скочила.
examples.en: Without a moment's delay, the fox jumped.

examples.sr: [Не ча̀сећи ни ча̏са], сео је на коња.
examples.en: Without a moment's delay, he got on his horse.

note: A fairy-tale formula for instant action. Sounds bookish in conversation.

meanings: for no reason (a joking answer to a silly question)

examples.sr: - Зашто? - [Збо̏г си̑ра].
examples.en: - Why? - Just because.

examples.sr: [Збо̏г си̑ра и во̑јне му̀зике], ништа више.
examples.en: Because of cheese and military music, and that's all.

note: A joking nonsense answer. There is also «због јотовања» (because of iotation): Serbian schoolchildren blame any illogical thing on grammar.

meanings: to separate the wheat from the chaff
forms: literally: to separate the wheat from the tares

examples.sr: Мора се знати [одва́јати жи̏то од ку̀коља].
examples.en: You have to know how to separate the wheat from the chaff.

examples.sr: Критичар [одва̀ја жи̏то од ку̀коља] у новој књизи.
examples.en: The critic separates the wheat from the chaff in the new book.

note: An image from field work; the meaning is the same as the English and biblical expression.

forms: literally: like an ace on a ten

examples.sr: То би ми дошло [ка̏о ке̑ц на де̏сет].
examples.en: That would be just what I need.

examples.sr: Аутобус је стигао [ка̏о ке̑ц на де̏сет].
examples.en: The bus arrived just in the nick of time.

note: Said of something that happens just in time: money when you need it, a bus at the door. «Кец» is an ace.

examples.sr: Ја сам [у ре̏бусу] шта да изаберем.
examples.en: I'm at a loss as to what to choose.

examples.sr: Цео свет је [у ре̏бусу].
examples.en: The whole world is baffled.

note: Colloquial: the person is tangled up as in a rebus puzzle and sees no way out.

examples.sr: Ти се загрејао, а ситуација се већ охладила - [ка̏сно па́ље̄ње].
examples.en: You got all worked up, but the situation had already cooled down - slow on the uptake.

examples.sr: Он је [ка̏сно па́ље̄ње], све схвати тек сутрадан.
examples.en: He's slow on the uptake, he only gets it the next day.

note: A joke about a slow thinker. Literally an auto mechanic's term.

examples.sr: На пољу цвета жута [у̀љана ре̏пица].
examples.en: Yellow rapeseed is blooming in the field.

examples.sr: Од [у̀љане ре̏пице] прави се јестиво уље.
examples.en: Cooking oil is made from rapeseed.

note: Literally «oil turnip»; that is what rapeseed is called in Serbian.

examples.sr: Данас је [ненаста̀вни да̑н] у школи.
examples.en: Today is a no-classes day at school.

examples.sr: Сутра је [ненаста̀вни да̑н], деца су код куће.
examples.en: Tomorrow is a non-teaching day, the kids are at home.

note: A day when school is closed that isn't called a vacation. «Наставни» means relating to teaching.

meanings: a promise only delights a fool
forms: literally: a promise to a fool - rejoicing

examples.sr: Знаш како кажу: [обећа́ње лу̑дом ра̏дова̄ње].
examples.en: You know what they say: a promise only delights a fool.

examples.sr: Ништа није урадио, само обећања - [обећа́ње лу̑дом ра̏дова̄ње].
examples.en: He hasn't done anything, only promises: a promise only delights a fool.

note: Empty promises please only the naive.

examples.sr: [Мо̀је пошто̀вање], господине директоре.
examples.en: My respects, Mr. Director.

examples.sr: Само [мо̀је пошто̀вање], немам речи.
examples.en: Hats off, I have no words.

note: A formal greeting instead of «добар дан»; in conversation, an expression of respect for someone's deed.

forms: literally: it goes on the nerves

examples.sr: Та бука ми [ѝде на жѝвце].
examples.en: That noise gets on my nerves.

examples.sr: Његово брбљање [ѝде на жѝвце] свима.
examples.en: His chatter gets on everybody's nerves.

note: «Живци» are nerves. Related «живцирати» - to irritate: «ја њу живцирам» - I annoy her.

meanings: birth certificate (an extract from the register)
forms: literally: extract from the register book of births

examples.sr: Треба ми [и̏звод из ма̀тичне књѝге ро̑ђених] за пасош.
examples.en: I need a birth certificate for my passport.

examples.sr: Где се издаје [и̏звод из ма̀тичне књѝге ро̑ђених]?
examples.en: Where is a birth certificate issued?

note: The official name of the document. In practice people just say «извод».

examples.sr: Дуго није смео да јој [иска̀же љу́бав].
examples.en: For a long time he didn't dare to declare his love to her.

examples.sr: Нушић је [иска̀зао љу́бав] другарици у школи.
examples.en: Nušić declared his love to a girl at school.

note: A bookish variant; in speech more often «рећи да неког волиш». Nušić has it in his «Аутобиографија».

examples.sr: - Ти си лењ! - [Ви̏ди ко̏ се ја̏вља]!
examples.en: - You're lazy! - Look who's talking!

examples.sr: [Ви̏ди ко̏ се ја̏вља], а ни он није бољи.
examples.en: Look who's talking, he's no better himself.

note: A retort to someone who is far from perfect themselves.

examples.sr: [Нѐмој да си ту́жан], проћи ће.
examples.en: Don't be sad, it will pass.

examples.sr: [Нѐмој да си] љут на мене.
examples.en: Don't be angry with me.

note: The negative imperative is «немој да» + present: «немој да журиш» (don't hurry), «немој да се мрдаш» (don't move).

meanings: the further south, the sadder (about the poverty of the southern regions)
forms: literally: the more southern, the sadder

examples.sr: У Србији важи: [што̏ ју̑жније, то̑ ту̑жније].
examples.en: In Serbia they say: the further south, the sadder.

note: Not about the weather: a saying about the weak economy of the southern regions of Serbia. In general: the further from the center, the worse.

key: phr:ко с ђаволом тикве сади, о главу му се разбијају
meanings: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas
whoever keeps bad company suffers for it
forms: literally: whoever plants pumpkins with the devil, they smash against his head

examples.sr: Знаш шта кажу: [ко̏ с ђа̏волом ти̏кве са̏ди, о гла̑ву му се разбѝјају].
examples.en: You know what they say: lie down with dogs, get up with fleas.

note: Often only the first half is said, «ко с ђаволом тикве сади»; everyone knows the rest.

meanings: to sing from the same hymn sheet
forms: literally: to blow into the same pumpkin

examples.sr: Њих двојица одувек [ду̏вају у ѝсту ти̏кву].
examples.en: The two of them have always sung from the same hymn sheet.

meanings: to be in cahoots with someone
to be in the same crowd as someone
forms: literally: to plant pumpkins with someone

examples.sr: Не волим да [са̏дим ти̏кве] са њим.
examples.en: I don't want to be in cahoots with him.

note: Usually negative: being in dubious company. Part of the proverb about the devil.

meanings: someone with no one to stand up for them
forms: literally: a pumpkin without a root

examples.sr: Он је [ти̏ква без ко̀рена], нема ко да га брани.
examples.en: He's a nobody with no connections, there's no one to defend him.

meanings: the spitting image of one's father

examples.sr: Дечак је [пљу̏нут о̀тац].
examples.en: The boy is the spitting image of his father.

note: Also «пљуната мајка». The image: the parent spat and a child came out. The adjective agrees with the gender.

meanings: a stage on the way to something

examples.sr: За њих је град био само [про̀лазна ста̀ница].
examples.en: For them the city was just a stopover.

examples.sr: Живе у [ди̏вљем бра̑ку] већ десет година.
examples.en: They have been living in a common-law marriage for ten years.

note: Cohabitation without a registered marriage.

forms: literally: a wedge is knocked out with a wedge

examples.sr: Ако те боли љубав, зна се: [кли̏н се кли̑ном избѝја].
examples.en: If love hurts, you know how it goes: one nail drives out another.

examples.sr: Верујеш ми, [жи̏ва и̏стина], не лажем.
examples.en: Believe me, it's the honest truth, I'm not lying.

note: Strengthens the word «истина» (truth). «Правда» means justice.

examples.sr: [Из то̏г ра̏злога] нисам дошао.
examples.en: For that reason I didn't come.

examples.sr: [Из ко̀јӣх ра̏злога] то радиш?
examples.en: For what reasons are you doing this?

forms: literally: to give the first goal

examples.sr: Тим је [да̑о пр̏ви го̑л] у првом полувремену.
examples.en: The team scored the first goal in the first half.

note: The score of a match is «резултат».

examples.sr: Обе екипе су [одѝграле нерѐшено].
examples.en: Both teams played to a draw.

examples.sr: Нова љубав му је [да̏ла но̑гу].
examples.en: His new girlfriend dumped him.

note: A colloquial expression for a breakup initiated by one side. Rare in writing.

forms: literally: a pregnant woman's sick leave

examples.sr: Била је на [тру̑дничком боло̀вању] од јуна.
examples.en: She has been on prenatal leave since June.

examples.sr: Добио сам књигу [на по̏клон].
examples.en: I was given a book as a gift.

note: Note the preposition «на»: «дати на поклон». Compare «поклонити» (to give as a gift).

examples.sr: Желим да разговарам с вама [у чѐтири о̀ка].
examples.en: I want to talk to you in private.

forms: literally: to breathe onto the mouth

examples.sr: Он спава и [ди̏ше на у̏ста].
examples.en: He sleeps and breathes through his mouth.

examples.sr: Купили су [ку̏ћу на спра̏т].
examples.en: They bought a two-story house.

note: A one-story house: «приземна кућа». «На спрат» means there is one floor above the ground floor.

examples.sr: За доручак желим [ја̀ја на о̏ко].
examples.en: I'd like fried eggs for breakfast.

forms: literally: on the account of the house

examples.sr: Пиће је [на ра̀чӯн ку̏ће].
examples.en: The drink is on the house.
